Pada 0 begins at 337.5°, the start of the North octant, so each compass octant holds four whole padas and a pada's quadrant is the octant direction/zone-from-bearing gives every bearing inside it. The devata names run in the Brihat Samhita 53.43-45 perimeter order, each side read clockwise from its corner, with Agni (the NE corner square) beginning at 45°; the same ring is served by entrance/pada and entrance/recommend. The 32-pada entrance grid, its bearings and its per-pada grades are later Vastu tradition, NOT a classical verse. Each pada labels its deity name and its quadrant separately: classical only where Brihat Samhita 53.43-48 (Iyer 1884, PD) names that devata and seats it on a perimeter square in that quadrant. The genuine verse-backed door rule is the 9-pada-per-side scheme of Manasara 38, surfaced below as classicalDoorScheme.

data.variantNote: 3 plan(s) generated and ranked by a weighted score of Vastu compliance (50%), usability (25%) and space efficiency (25%). The top-level rooms / mandala / compliance / svg are the recommended variant — "vastu-first". Identical layouts are returned once, so fewer than the requested number can come back. Drawings are included unless "includeSvg": false; with drawings enabled, send "variantSvg": true to render every option (adds roughly 20 KB each). The 9-zone `mandala` is plot geometry and is identical for every variant, so it is returned once at the top level. When every option scores the SAME Vastu compliance, the classical (vastu-first) plan is recommended regardless of the other two axes.

87% of the buildable area is occupied by rooms (2084.8 of 2400 sq units)
usabilityFactors: -12 1 bedroom(s) sit next to the E entrance zone — no privacy buffer

variants.strategyNote: Rooms claim their prescribed zone in product placement priority order (pooja, kitchen, master bedroom, then the rest). Maximises the compliance index; may put a bedroom next to the front door.
